title: Built-in tools section predates v2.3 downloadable packages
reality: v2.3.0 moved Hierarchical Maps, Conversation Calls, UNO, Chess, Poker, 8-Ball Pool, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Rock-Paper-Scissors into optional downloadable packages with package-owned server runtimes, cutting >25,000 lines from the base Engine; the base now exposes capability registries and packages supply feature code on demand. Music player controls (Spotify/YouTube/Custom) now show 'Download Music DJ Agent to configure' guidance and only function with Music DJ installed (2.3.0). Capability API 1.3 (2.3.2 #3690) gives packages safe model routing, persistence, resources, logging, and client contribution loading. So the fixed '~18 built-in tools' roster in tool-executor.ts is no longer the whole story — several tool surfaces are now package-owned and only present when their package is installed.
fix: In the 'Built-In Tools' section of references/custom-tools.md, add a v2.3 note: the base Engine was slimmed in 2.3.0 and optional agent/game/call/map tooling now ships as downloadable packages (Agents -> Download Agents, Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents catalog); package-owned tools/commands register only while their package is installed. Flag the Spotify/music tool bullet as dependent on the Music DJ package being installed. Keep core tools (roll_dice, update_game_state, lorebook tools, chat summary/variable tools, update_about_me) listed as true Engine built-ins.

title: No coverage of package-owned slash commands and no-restart activation
reality: As of 2.3.0, the six table games appear directly in Conversation Commands controls without separate Add Agent entries, Conversation command controls were consolidated under Chat Settings -> Agents, and package-owned command toggles appear only for installed agents. As of 2.3.2 (#3699), installed Conversation games appear immediately in slash-command autocomplete and activate/deactivate their command and runtime contributions without an Engine restart (route-bearing packages keep a safe restart path).
fix: Add a short 'Package-owned commands (v2.3)' subsection to references/custom-tools.md (near Built-In Tools or UI Location) explaining: table-game and other package commands live in Chat Settings Commands controls, appear only when the owning package is installed, and installed Conversation games activate their slash commands without an Engine restart (#3699, 2.3.2); command toggles for uninstalled packages are hidden (2.3.0).

title: Illustrator gating of /illustrate, /selfie, and Gallery generation actions undocumented
reality: In 2.3.0 the Connections 'Illustrator' defaults category was renamed 'Images', and image/video generation settings plus the /illustrate and /selfie slash commands are hidden until the Illustrator package is installed. Gallery generation controls (Illustrate, Selfie, Storyboard, Video, Animate, Background) now require Illustrator to be installed AND enabled for that chat in every mode (2.3.0 fixed). A 2.3.2 fix ensures the Selfies command toggle reappears alongside Illustrator settings once the package is installed. Selfie prompt generation routes through the per-chat Prompt Model selection (#3638, 2.3.0).
fix: Add a note to references/custom-tools.md (in the new package-owned commands subsection or Built-In Tools): /illustrate and /selfie are hidden and Gallery Illustrate/Selfie/Storyboard/Video/Animate/Background actions are unavailable unless the Illustrator package is installed and enabled for the chat (2.3.0); the Connections defaults category formerly called 'Illustrator' is now 'Images'. Users asking why these commands are missing should be told to install Illustrator from Download Agents.

title: update_about_me entry missing v2.3 built-in status and Professor Mari drafting move
reality: 2.3.0 explicitly states Conversation mode's About Me profile and the update_about_me tool remain built into the Engine and are NOT downloadable agents (unlike most optional capabilities that moved to packages). In 2.3.2, About Me drafting moved from the per-editor 'AI Write' controls to Professor Mari: Character and Persona Convo editors no longer expose a separate model connection or source settings; Mari inspects a saved character or persona, writes the bio in their voice, and saves it directly to the real About Me field.
fix: Extend the update_about_me bullet in references/custom-tools.md Built-In Tools: add '(still built into the Engine in the v2.3 downloadable-agents era — not a downloadable package, per 2.3.0)' and note that as of 2.3.2 About Me bio DRAFTING is done via Professor Mari rather than the removed per-editor AI Write controls, while the update_about_me tool itself is unchanged (opt-in, Conversation-only, public scope needs user approval).

title: Timeout discussion should distinguish new CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS
reality: 2.3.3 (#3730) added CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS for slow Conversation, Roleplay, and Game text-generation providers (and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false for launcher update opt-out). This is a separate knob from the custom-tool timeout; users tuning timeouts for tool-heavy setups may conflate the two.
fix: In references/custom-tools.md where CUSTOM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS is described (webhook/script sections or Best Practices), add a one-line cross-reference: chat generation itself has its own timeout env var, CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS (2.3.3, #3730), distinct from CUSTOM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS which only bounds tool execution.

title: 'No central marketplace yet' now misleading without Download Agents cross-reference
reality: CSS/JS client extensions are still manually installed, but since 2.3.0 Marinara has an official Agents -> Download Agents full-page library backed by the verified first-party Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents catalog (Writer/Tracker/Misc/Maps/Calls/game packages, Install All/Uninstall All), with automatic startup upgrades of installed packages (2.3.1) and compatibility-aware per-major catalog lanes (2.3.3 #3712). Downloadable agent packages are a separate distribution channel from client extensions, but a reader of the current 'There's no central marketplace yet' line would wrongly conclude Marinara has no official package catalog at all.
fix: In references/extensions.md 'Installation and Distribution', rewrite the opening line to: there is no marketplace for CLIENT EXTENSIONS — they remain manual JSON/CSS/JS or zip import — but since v2.3.0 an official Download Agents catalog (Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents) distributes verified capability PACKAGES (agents, maps, calls, games); extensions and downloadable agent packages are distinct surfaces — do not conflate them; cross-reference agents.md for the catalog.

title: 'Fork the engine' escape hatch outdated by capability packages
reality: The 'What Extensions CAN'T Do' section ends with 'If you need any of these, fork the engine.' Since 2.3.0, optional features ship as downloadable capability packages with package-owned server runtimes AND client surfaces, and capability API 1.3 (2.3.2 #3690) provides host services for packages: safe model routing, persistence, history/checkpoints, resources, logging, transactions, and client contribution loading. The Marinara-Agents repo (2.3.0) has public contribution rules, templates, catalog validation, and a protected review flow — so server-side behavior or new surfaces can be delivered as a verified package rather than a fork.
fix: In references/extensions.md 'What Extensions CAN'T Do', replace the bare 'fork the engine' conclusion with: for server-side runtimes, new commands/surfaces, or agent-like behavior, the v2.3 path is building a downloadable capability package against capability API 1.3 (2.3.2 #3690) and contributing it via the Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents repo; forking is only needed for changes the capability API cannot express.

title: Extension-vs-other-surfaces decision list missing downloadable package option
reality: The 'When to Use Extensions vs. Other Surfaces' list covers Extension / Custom Agent / Custom Tool / Character card / Lorebook, but v2.3.0 introduced a sixth surface: downloadable capability packages (package-owned server runtime + client surface + slash commands, installed from Download Agents).
fix: Add a line to the surfaces list in references/extensions.md: 'Downloadable Agent package (v2.3) — installable capability with its own server runtime, client surface, and commands; check Download Agents before hand-building an extension or agent, and see agents.md.'
